extra.message: OS command injection in ops shell probe endpoint — Arbitrary OS command execution on the server [verified: host is concatenated directly into os.system with no sanitization, so shell metacharacters achieve command injection.]

Path traversal (arbitrary file write) in ops dock shelf endpoint — Arbitrary file write, potentially leading to remote code execution or data corruption [verified: name is joined to BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no sanitization and the raw body is written there, allowing arbitrary file write/overwrite.]

Hardcoded default JWT SECRET_KEY not enforced in production — If deployed with the default key, an attacker can forge valid JWTs for any user including admin, achieving full auth bypass. [verified: SECRET_KEY has a hardcoded, publicly-known default used to sign/verify JWTs (core/security.py), and there is no startup check rejecting this default when ENVIRONMENT is not 'development', so a misconfigured deployment silently signs tokens with a known key enabling full auth bypass.]

Path traversal (arbitrary file read) in ops parcel endpoint — Arbitrary file read from the server filesystem [verified: packet_ref is joined to BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no normalization/containment check, so '../' or absolute paths escape the directory for arbitrary file read.]

SSRF in ops relay bridge endpoint — Access to internal network services or cloud metadata endpoints from the server [verified: url is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen with no allow-list, enabling SSRF to internal hosts/metadata endpoints.]

Code injection via eval() in ops formula endpoint — Remote code execution / sandbox escape leading to full server compromise [verified: eval() with data-only inputs still permits DoS/arbitrary arithmetic and is a code-injection anti-pattern reachable behind only a static shared-secret header, not real user auth.]

CORS misconfiguration reflecting Origin with credentials enabled — Any malicious website can make authenticated cross-origin requests and read responses, enabling CSRF-style data theft [verified: Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set true, permitting any origin credentialed cross-site reads.]

Hardcoded/guessable privilege badge bypass — Trivial privilege escalation to view sensitive payroll/casework data by sending a static header value [verified: Elevated payroll/casework data is granted purely on a client-supplied cookie/header equal to the static unsigned string 'lead' with no cryptographic binding to a session.]

NoSQL injection in ops mongo lookup endpoint — Unauthorized data retrieval or query-logic bypass against the backing MongoDB store [verified: payload['filter'] or the raw payload is passed unmodified to find_one() with no schema/type restriction, allowing NoSQL operator injection.]

XXE in ops XML fold endpoint — Local file disclosure, SSRF, or denial of service via XML entity expansion [verified: XMLParser is configured with load_dtd=True and resolve_entities=True on attacker-supplied body, enabling classic XXE file read/SSRF.]

Unauthenticated static file mount exposes uploaded borrower documents — Unauthenticated attacker can read any borrower's uploaded KYC/financial documents (IDs, bank statements, tax returns) by guessing or enumerating filenames, since the filename pattern doc_{doc_id}_{YYYYmmddHHMMSS}{ext} is predictable/brute-forceable and bypasses the authenticated /api/documents download endpoint entirely. [verified: main.py:36 mounts uploads/ via StaticFiles with no auth dependency, while documents.py:127-129 saves files with predictable names doc_{doc_id}_{timestamp}{ext}; anyone can fetch them directly bypassing the require_user+ownership check in the /api/documents/{doc_id}/download route.]

Borrower can self-approve/self-reject loan application, bypassing underwriting — A borrower can escalate their own loan application straight to 'approved' (or 'rejected') status without any underwriter decision being made, bypassing the entire underwriting/decisioning process and potentially causing unauthorized loan approval. [verified: Borrower edit gate at lines 199-203 only checks status, not target status; VALID_TRANSITIONS allows counteroffered->approved/rejected and the only extra gate (223-229) checks document completeness, not decision authority, so a borrower can PUT status=approved on their own application.]

Unvalidated file extension derived from client-controlled filename during document upload — An attacker can upload a file with a spoofed Content-Type header (e.g. claiming application/pdf) but supply a dangerous extension such as .html/.svg/.js in the original filename; combined with the public /uploads static mount, this can be used to host attacker-controlled content (e.g. stored XSS via an uploaded .html/.svg file) served from the application's own origin. [verified: main.py:36 mounts settings.UPLOAD_DIR as static /uploads, and documents.py:128 takes the extension straight from client-supplied file.filename with only the spoofable content_type checked — an uploaded .html/.svg is stored and served as static content from the app origin, enabling stored XSS.]

Missing ownership/assignment check on document download for staff roles — Unassigned staff can download any borrower's sensitive uploaded documents (ID scans, financial statements) [verified: download_document only checks ownership when role==borrower (documents.py:150-152); underwriter/support/admin branches have no assignment check, so any staff account can download any document by ID.]

Open redirect in ops lane endpoint — Phishing via redirect to attacker-controlled domains from a trusted host [verified: lane is passed unchecked into RedirectResponse with no relative-path/allow-list validation, enabling open redirect.]

Mass assignment in ops workset rebind endpoint — Attacker can set privileged/internal fields (role, approval status) that should not be client-controlled [verified: workset.update(payload) merges the full client JSON into a dict containing role/approved/balance with no field allow-list, letting a caller set any of those keys in the response.]

Insecure cookie flags on ops portal_crumb cookie — Cookie theft via XSS or network interception due to missing Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite [verified: set_cookie is called with no secure/httponly/samesite flags, unlike the app's real auth cookie handling, allowing JS access and plaintext transmission.]

Predictable shared temporary password for bulk-imported borrowers — Anyone aware of the well-known default password can log into any freshly bulk-imported borrower account before it's changed, accessing their loan data. [verified: hashed_password=get_password_hash("TempPass123!") is identical for every imported user with no forced-reset flag or expiry, so anyone learning it can access freshly imported borrower accounts.]

CSV formula injection in admin exports — Arbitrary formula/macro execution in the spreadsheet app of the staff member who opens the exported CSV, potentially leading to code execution, data exfiltration, or credential theft on an internal admin workstation [verified: rows built from app.purpose/business_name are passed straight to csv.DictWriter with no escaping of leading =/+/-/@, and these fields are attacker-controlled via application/registration input.]

CSV formula injection in decisions export — Formula/macro execution in the spreadsheet application of whoever opens the exported decisions CSV [verified: Same unsanitized csv.DictWriter sink at line 223 writes borrower business_name and reasons/conditions without escaping formula-trigger characters.]

Unauthenticated IDOR exposing loan application status — Unauthenticated attackers can enumerate application IDs and disclose loan status/PII-adjacent data for any borrower. [verified: The /status/{app_id} route only depends on get_db with no require_user/auth dependency, unlike every sibling endpoint in the file, so any unauthenticated caller can enumerate app_id and read status/timestamp for any borrower application.]

Auth cookie missing Secure flag — Network attackers on unencrypted connections can capture the access_token cookie and hijack borrower/staff sessions. [verified: auth.py:46 explicitly sets secure=False on the access_token cookie, so it will be sent over plaintext HTTP allowing network attackers to capture it and hijack sessions.]

Internal document review notes leaked to borrowers — Borrowers see confidential internal underwriting notes and rejection rationale not intended for them [verified: list_documents (documents.py:63-74) returns review_notes and rejection_reason unconditionally for every role including borrowers, with no field filtering by role.]

Any underwriter can review/reject documents on unassigned applications — Unauthorized underwriter can approve or reject documents/loan outcomes for applications outside their assignment, undermining underwriting integrity [verified: review_document only checks role in (underwriter, admin) (documents.py:174) with no check against application.assigned_underwriter_id, letting any underwriter review/reject documents on unassigned applications.]

Missing per-application authorization on underwriting notes — Any underwriter/support/admin can read internal case notes for any application, not just ones assigned to them [verified: list_notes checks ownership only when current_user.role == borrower (line 29); underwriter/support/admin get no assignment or scoping check at all, so any authenticated staff user can pull internal notes for any app_id by iterating IDs.]

Unrestricted/unvalidated file upload in borrower bulk import — Denial of service via unbounded memory consumption or crash from oversized/malformed uploaded file [verified: admin.py:83 reads the entire uploaded file into memory and decodes it with no size limit, content-type, or extension check, unlike documents.py's ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES/MAX_FILE_SIZE controls, allowing an oversized/malformed file to crash or exhaust memory. Impact is limited since it requires an authenticated admin role, so severity is low rather than the reported DoS being high-impact.]

Underwriters/support can view unassigned applications' PII — Over-broad internal access exposes borrower SSNs and financials to staff without a legitimate need-to-know, increasing insider-threat risk. [verified: The `pass` at line 103 is a genuine no-op — any underwriter/support_specialist can view full PII of any application regardless of assignment, confirmed missing control. Severity is low since this is intra-staff (authenticated internal roles), not external exposure.]

Internal underwriting reasons leaked to borrowers — Borrowers can view confidential internal underwriting notes/rationale not meant for them, risking compliance/fair-lending exposure. [verified: get_decision_for_application only checks ownership, then returns _decision_dict which includes internal_reasons (line 29) unconditionally, whereas applications.py's decision_dict (lines 146-157) deliberately excludes internal_reasons for the same borrower-facing context, confirming the field should be filtered here too.]
